story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Spotlight

Vaathiyaar shines a spotlight on a crowded room. "When you read 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired', which word does 'it' refer to? You attend to 'cat', not 'mat'. Attention lets the model do the same."

### Self-Attention: Query, Key, Value

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import math

class SelfAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, embed_dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.W_q = nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)  # Query
        self.W_k = nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)  # Key
        self.W_v = nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)  # Value
        self.scale = math.sqrt(embed_dim)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        Q = self.W_q(x)  # What am I looking for?
        K = self.W_k(x)  # What do I contain?
        V = self.W_v(x)  # What information do I provide?
        
        # Attention scores: how much should each position attend to each other?
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / self.scale
        attention_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        
        # Weighted sum of values
        output = torch.matmul(attention_weights, V)
        return output, attention_weights

# Example: batch=1, seq_len=5, embed_dim=8
x = torch.randn(1, 5, 8)
attn = SelfAttention(8)
output, weights = attn(x)

print(f'Input shape: {x.shape}')          # [1, 5, 8]
print(f'Output shape: {output.shape}')     # [1, 5, 8]
print(f'Attention weights: {weights.shape}') # [1, 5, 5]
print(f'Weights sum per row: {weights.sum(dim=-1)}')  # all 1.0
```

### Multi-Head Attention

```python
class MultiHeadAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, embed_dim, num_heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
        self.attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads, batch_first=True)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        output, weights = self.attention(x, x, x)  # self-attention: Q=K=V=x
        return output, weights

mha = MultiHeadAttention(embed_dim=64, num_heads=8)
x = torch.randn(2, 10, 64)  # batch=2, seq=10, dim=64
out, w = mha(x)
print(f'Multi-head output: {out.shape}')  # [2, 10, 64]
```

> **Key Insight:** Attention lets each token look at ALL other tokens and decide which are relevant. This is why transformers process sequences so well — no information bottleneck!
story_variants.ta:
## வாத்தியாரின் ஸ்பாட்லைட்

வாத்தியார் நிறைந்த அறையில் ஸ்பாட்லைட் பாய்ச்சுகிறார். "'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired' என்று படிக்கும்போது, 'it' எந்த வார்த்தையைக் குறிக்கிறது? நீங்கள் 'cat'-ல் கவனம் செலுத்துகிறீர்கள், 'mat' அல்ல. Attention மாதிரிக்கு அதையே செய்ய அனுமதிக்கிறது."

explanation.en: Query projection: 'What am I looking for?' Each token creates a query vector
Key projection: 'What do I contain?' Each token advertises its content
Value projection: 'What info do I provide?' The actual content to aggregate
Project all tokens to query space. Shape: [batch, seq_len, embed_dim]
Dot product of Q and K gives attention scores. Scale by sqrt(d) for stability
Softmax normalizes scores to probabilities. Each row sums to 1.0
Weighted sum of values: each token gets a blend of all tokens weighted by attention
PyTorch built-in: runs multiple attention heads in parallel, each learning different patterns
Self-attention: Q=K=V=x. Each token attends to all tokens in the same sequence

steps.line: # 8 heads of dim 8 each = 64 total (same as single head of 64)

explanation.en: Multi-head: instead of one 64-dim attention, use 8 parallel 8-dim attentions. Different perspectives!

animation_sequence.code:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import math

def scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V):
    d_k = Q.size(-1)
    scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(d_k)
    weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    return torch.matmul(weights, V), weights

# Example: 1 head, seq_len=4, d_k=8
Q = torch.randn(1, 4, 8)
K = torch.randn(1, 4, 8)
V = torch.randn(1, 4, 8)

output, attn_weights = scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V)
print(f'Output shape: {output.shape}')
print(f'Attention weights: {attn_weights.shape}')
print(f'Weights sum per query: {attn_weights.sum(dim=-1)}')

executionSteps.explanation: Core attention mechanism: Q, K, V
Compute similarity scores, scale by sqrt(d_k)
Softmax converts scores to probabilities (sum to 1)
Weighted sum of values — attend to relevant keys
Same shape as input — enriched with context
Each query's attention weights sum to 1

instruction.en: PyTorch cannot run in this sandbox, so this is the numpy version of what PyTorch does under the hood. Implement self-attention from scratch. `softmax(x, axis=-1)` must be numerically stable (subtract the max). `scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V, mask=None)` computes scores = Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k) (d_k = K.shape[-1]); where a boolean `mask` is False, set the score to -1e9 so it gets no attention; weights = softmax(scores) over the last axis; return (weights @ V, weights). `self_attention(X, Wq, Wk, Wv)` projects X into Q = X @ Wq, K = X @ Wk, V = X @ Wv and calls it. The program prints the 6x6 attention weights for 'the cat sat on the mat' and which word each word attends to most.
instruction.ta: இந்த sandbox-ல் PyTorch இயங்காது, எனவே இது PyTorch உள்ளே செய்வதன் numpy பதிப்பு. Self-attention-ஐ புதிதாக எழுதுங்கள். `softmax(x, axis=-1)` எண்ணியல் ரீதியாக நிலையானதாக இருக்க வேண்டும் (max-ஐக் கழியுங்கள்). `scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V, mask=None)` scores = Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k) (d_k = K.shape[-1]) கணக்கிடுகிறது; boolean `mask` False ஆக உள்ள இடங்களில் score-ஐ -1e9 ஆக்குங்கள், அப்போது அவற்றுக்கு attention கிடைக்காது; weights = கடைசி axis மீது softmax(scores); (weights @ V, weights) திருப்புங்கள். `self_attention(X, Wq, Wk, Wv)` X-ஐ Q = X @ Wq, K = X @ Wk, V = X @ Wv என project செய்து அதை அழைக்கிறது. 'the cat sat on the mat'-க்கான 6x6 attention weights-ஐயும், ஒவ்வொரு சொல்லும் அதிகம் கவனிக்கும் சொல்லையும் program அச்சிடுகிறது.

import numpy as np
_s = softmax(np.array([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0], [1000.0, 1000.0, 1000.0]]))
assert _s is not None and np.allclose(_s.sum(axis=-1), 1.0), "softmax rows must sum to 1"
assert np.allclose(_s[1], 1 / 3), "softmax must stay stable for large values - subtract the max"
_rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
_Q, _K, _V = _rng.standard_normal((3, 8)), _rng.standard_normal((5, 8)), _rng.standard_normal((5, 2))
_res = scaled_dot_product_attention(_Q, _K, _V)
assert isinstance(_res, tuple) and len(_res) == 2, "scaled_dot_product_attention must return (output, weights)"
_out, _w = _res
assert np.shape(_w) == (3, 5) and np.shape(_out) == (3, 2), "weights must be (queries, keys) and output (queries, value_dim)"
_sc = _Q @ _K.T / np.sqrt(8)
_ref = np.exp(_sc - _sc.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)); _ref /= _ref.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
assert np.allclose(_w, _ref), "weights must be softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) - remember the sqrt(d_k) scaling"
assert np.allclose(_out, _ref @ _V), "the output must be weights @ V"
_X = _rng.standard_normal((4, 3))
_mask = np.tril(np.ones((4, 4), dtype=bool))
_o2, _w2 = scaled_dot_product_attention(_X, _X, _X, mask=_mask)
assert np.allclose(np.triu(_w2, k=1), 0.0) and np.allclose(_w2.sum(axis=1), 1.0), "where the mask is False the weight must be 0 (and rows still sum to 1)"
_W = [_rng.standard_normal((3, 3)) for _ in range(3)]
_sa = self_attention(_X, *_W)
assert _sa is not None and np.allclose(_sa[0], scaled_dot_product_attention(_X @ _W[0], _X @ _W[1], _X @ _W[2])[0]), "self_attention must use Q = X @ Wq, K = X @ Wk, V = X @ Wv"
print("All attention tests passed!")

under_the_hood.summary: In code, attention is a few tensor operations: project the batch into Q, K and V with linear layers, take Q @ Kᵀ scaled by sqrt(d), fill masked positions with minus infinity, softmax over the last dimension, and multiply by V.

steps.title: Linear layers make Q, K and V
steps.body: For input x of shape (batch, seq, embed), self.W_q(x), self.W_k(x) and self.W_v(x) each return (batch, seq, embed). Every token gets three learned views of itself: what it is looking for, how it can be found, and what it will contribute.

steps.title: Scores are a batched matrix product
steps.body: scores = Q @ K.transpose(-2, -1) / math.sqrt(embed) has shape (batch, seq, seq): entry [b, i, j] says how much token i attends to token j in example b. For 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired', the row for 'it' should end up highest at 'cat'.

props.caption: Tensor shapes through one attention call

steps.title: Masks set scores to minus infinity
steps.body: Before softmax, positions a token must not see are filled with -inf, because e^-inf = 0. For a causal mask, token 2 with scores [0.5, 1.5, 2.0] against tokens 1 to 3 becomes [0.5, 1.5, -inf], and softmax gives [0.27, 0.73, 0]: no peeking at the future. Padding masks use the same trick to ignore filler tokens.

steps.title: Softmax over the last dimension
steps.body: F.softmax(scores, dim=-1) normalises each row so that one token's attention weights over all keys sum to 1. Using the wrong dim would normalise over queries instead, a subtle bug that still runs. The result times V mixes value vectors according to those weights.

steps.title: Reading attention maps
steps.body: Returning the weight tensor lets you plot a seq x seq heatmap per head. It shows where information came from, not why the model decided something, so treat it as a clue rather than an explanation. PyTorch's F.scaled_dot_product_attention computes the same result with fused, memory-efficient kernels.

nodes.label: Q, K, V = W_q x, W_k x, W_v x

under_the_hood.takeaway: Attention in code is matmul, scale, mask, softmax, matmul. Keep the shapes (batch, seq, seq) for weights and (batch, seq, embed) for outputs in mind, and remember that masks work by sending scores to minus infinity.
